title: Design Nearby Friends / Proximity Service
prompt: Design a 'Nearby Friends' feature: users who opt in continuously share their location, and each user sees which of their friends are within a configurable radius (say 5 km), updated in near real time. Cover how you ingest high-frequency location updates and how you answer proximity queries at scale.
blurb: The canonical geospatial fan-out problem — indexing moving points with geohash/quadtree, ingesting a firehose of location pings, and pushing proximity changes to friends in real time.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (opt-in sharing, radius query, friend-scoped, real-time push) from non-functional (freshness < ~10s, privacy, availability, battery/bandwidth on client).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about active-user count, update frequency, radius size, friend graph size, freshness SLA, whether it is friend-scoped vs global nearby.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Derives location-update QPS (users x ping rate), fan-out volume, index memory footprint, and read/query QPS.

rubric.label: Geospatial indexing depth
rubric.description: Geohash vs quadtree vs S2 vs H3; precision/cell-size tradeoff, boundary/neighbor-cell problem, index update cost for moving points.

rubric.label: Location ingestion path
rubric.description: Handles a write-heavy firehose: stateless ingestion tier, location cache (Redis GEO / in-memory), TTL on stale locations, avoiding write amplification.

rubric.label: Fan-out & real-time delivery
rubric.description: Friend-scoped push via websockets/pubsub; compute proximity on write vs on read; only emit on state change (entered/left radius).

rubric.label: High-level design
rubric.description: Client -> LB -> location ingestion -> location store/cache -> proximity engine -> pub/sub -> websocket gateway -> friends; friend-graph service.

rubric.label: Scaling
rubric.description: Shard by geo cell and/or user; handle dense cells (stadiums), redistribute hot cells, horizontal websocket gateways with a session registry.

rubric.label: Bottlenecks
rubric.description: Identifies dense-cell hotspots, fan-out amplification for users with many friends, and stale-location cleanup.

rubric.label: Privacy & security
rubric.description: Opt-in, granular sharing, location precision/blurring, revocation, not leaking location to non-friends, retention limits.

rubric.label: Observability
rubric.description: Freshness/staleness metrics, delivery latency, dropped-update rate, hot-cell alerts, connection churn.

functional_requirements: Users opt in to share live location
A user sees friends currently within radius R
Near-real-time updates as friends move in/out of radius
nonfunctional_requirements: Freshness: nearby set reflects reality within ~5-10s
High availability for reads; updates can be lossy (last-write-wins)
Low client battery/bandwidth cost (adaptive ping rate)
Horizontally scalable to tens of millions of active sharers
clarifying_questions: How many concurrent users share location, and at what ping frequency?
Is 'nearby' friend-scoped only, or also strangers/places?
What radius, and is it user-configurable?
How fresh must the nearby set be (SLA)?
Average and p99 friend-count per user (fan-out sizing)?
Do we persist location history or only the latest point?
qualifying_questions: Is it acceptable to drop/merge rapid updates (eventual freshness)?
Global audience with regional data residency requirements?
Do we need entered/left events or just a periodic nearby list?

estimations.traffic: 10M active sharers pinging every 5s = 2M location updates/s. If we down-sample server-side to every 30s effective, ~330K writes/s to the index.
estimations.fanout: Avg 200 friends/user; only friends who are (a) online and (b) near matter. Proximity change events are far fewer than raw pings — emit only on radius crossings.
estimations.index_memory: 10M users x ~100B (id, lat, lng, ts, geohash) ~= 1GB hot in a distributed in-memory store; trivially shardable.
estimations.read_qps: If clients also poll, cap by pushing deltas over persistent connections instead of polling.

core_components: Location store/cache (Redis GEO or in-memory geo-index)
data_model: locations(user_id PK, lat, lng, geohash, updated_at TTL)
api_design: WS /subscribe -> server pushes { friend_id, distance, entered|left, ts }
GET /nearby?radius=5000 -> snapshot list of nearby friends
reference.high_level_design: Clients push location to a stateless ingestion tier behind the LB. Ingestion writes latest position to a geo-indexed store (Redis GEO / geohash buckets) with a TTL so stale sharers age out. A proximity engine, on each update, looks up the user's friends (from the friend-graph service), checks which are within R using the geo index, and emits only entered/left transitions to a pub/sub topic keyed by user. WebSocket gateways subscribe on behalf of connected clients (session registry maps user -> gateway node) and push deltas. Sharing/consent is checked before any location is stored or revealed.

deep_dives.probe: Geohash vs quadtree vs S2/H3 for indexing moving points? How do you pick cell precision, and how do you handle two friends near a cell boundary who are close in reality but in different cells?
Do you compute proximity on write (per location update, scan friends) or on read (per query)? What changes when a user has 5000 friends vs 20?
A concert packs 100K sharers into a few cells. How do you keep that cell from becoming a hotspot in both index writes and query fan-out?
How do WebSocket gateways scale horizontally, and how does a location update reach the right gateway holding a friend's connection?

Product wants a location-history / 'were we ever near?' feature. Your latest-location cache only holds the current point. How would you stream position changes out to a history/analytics store — change data capture, Debezium off the datastore, or explicit event emission?
How do you ensure a friend who lost signal or closed the app disappears from nearby lists — TTL, tombstones, heartbeat?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions geohash or quadtree or s2 or h3
followup_bank.question: What cell precision, and how do you handle the boundary problem where nearby points fall in adjacent cells — search the 8 neighbor cells?
What is your eviction/TTL policy for stale locations, and how do you avoid a stampede when a hot cell's entries all expire and refill at once?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions database or postgres or cassandra or sql
followup_bank.question: If you persist positions or history in a datastore, how do you capture changes downstream for analytics — CDC/Debezium vs dual writes?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions websocket or push or pubsub
followup_bank.question: How does an update for user A reach the specific gateway node holding friend B's live connection? Describe the session registry / routing.
For a user with thousands of friends, do you fan out on write or read, and how do you bound the cost?

scaling: Shard the geo index by cell (geohash prefix) and the session registry by user_id
Redistribute or sub-shard dense cells (stadium/concert) dynamically
Emit only radius-crossing transitions, not every ping
Down-sample ingestion server-side; adaptive client ping rate based on movement
Stateless ingestion and gateways scale horizontally behind a session registry
bottlenecks: WebSocket connection churn and reconnect storms
tradeoffs: Compute-on-write (fresh, costly per ping) vs compute-on-read (cheap writes, staler)
Geohash (simple, boundary issues) vs quadtree/S2 (adaptive density, more complex)
Push deltas (efficient, stateful conns) vs poll (simple, chatty)
Higher ping rate (fresher) vs battery/bandwidth cost
alternative_solutions: Redis GEO commands (GEOADD/GEOSEARCH) as the index
PostGIS with spatial index for lower-scale/analytics
S2 cell covering + Kafka-partitioned proximity workers
Grid bucketing in memory with neighbor-cell scan
observability: Connection count and reconnect churn per gateway
security: Rate-limit and authenticate location writes to prevent spoofing
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer scopes freshness and privacy, sizes the update firehose and fan-out, and picks a geospatial index (geohash/quadtree/S2) with an explicit boundary-cell story. It ingests via a stateless tier into a TTL'd geo cache, computes proximity on write emitting only entered/left transitions, and routes deltas through pub/sub to horizontally scaled WebSocket gateways via a session registry. It proactively raises dense-cell hotspots and high-friend fan-out as the main bottlenecks, and treats consent/precision/retention as first-class.

interviewer_notes: Let the candidate scope privacy and freshness before diving in. The core differentiator is the geospatial index — push hard on cell precision and the boundary problem; a senior candidate mentions neighbor-cell search or adaptive cells (quadtree/S2). If they place a datastore for history, interrupt with the CDC/Debezium probe. If they add Redis/cache, probe TTL for stale locations and stampede on hot cells. Make them reason about compute-on-write vs on-read and about dense-cell hotspots. Reserve the last minutes for real-time delivery routing (session registry) and privacy/consent.
